name: ANGDA Glennallen to Palmer Spur Line

values.PipelineName: ANGDA Glennallen to Palmer Spur Line

researcher_notes: The Alaska Natural Gas Development Authority filed a right-of-way lease application dated April 4, 2005 with the State of Alaska for a buried 24-inch steel gas pipeline of about 148 miles from Glennallen to just west of Palmer, with a stated capacity of 1,000 million standard cubic feet per day. The application is the concrete step. The sponsor is a State of Alaska public corporation. Search results from the Alaska Division of Oil and Gas show a native lands report supporting a conditional right-of-way lease application, and a Petroleum News piece from September 2006 discusses the spur line, but neither was read for the length. A later Alaska Division of Oil and Gas summary calls it 143 miles; the application itself says 148. No sign of construction, a start year, or activity after about 2008 was found, so the status shelved with type inferred is a presumption and no URL backs it. Status needs a check by a person. The applicant is not in the owner list; the entity lookup found no exact match and the style tool found no legal form. Route not found, so no route is proposed. Only one source states the values, so the tier is medium. Extra context pages that load: https://dog.dnr.alaska.gov/Documents/SPCS/ANGDA/FinalReports/MiscellaneousReports/NativeLandReport.pdf and https://www.petroleumnews.com/pntruncate/28843979.shtml. The start location was recorded from the application text, which says the line begins in Glennallen on Ahtna lands.
